tasks.short: Collect environmental evidence and analyse restoration needs

steps.what: Collect environmental data and verify observations, sampling context and analysis definitions
Analyze data through specified summary calculations and spatial comparison views
Determine environmental conditions and restoration needs by interpreting results, uncertainty and ecological context

tasks.design: Configure repeated summaries and spatial views in an {OTHER} environmental field-data and geospatial analysis environment after the planner checks collected evidence. Keep observations and assessment limits in {DOCS}; the planner determines restoration needs rather than accepting a computed ecological-status flag.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated preparation of summaries and maps occupied time between collecting observations and interpreting restoration needs.
tasks.enabler_now: Native analytical configuration can reuse explicit calculation and mapping definitions.
tasks.still_hard: Measurements may not represent seasonal variability, ecological interactions or the relevant restoration mechanism.
tasks.human_edge: The planner recognises where more observation is needed before recommending intervention.
tasks.altitude: Some analysis preparation may fall; field collection and ecological interpretation retain their time.

reach.task: Assess whether observations represent the habitat condition

evidence.claim: Copernicus Data Space supports rerunnable Earth observation analysis; this supports a possible spatial-analysis component, not replacement of field collection or ecological assessment.
The proposed summary-preparation saving is an unmeasured model-knowledge scenario.

assumptions: Boundary includes planner collection, analytical preparation and needs assessment; other field staff labour remains outside the focal denominator and receives no saving.

In fully retained s1 the planner collects and checks sample id, location, time, method, parameter, result, unit, source and observation limits, then defines summaries and spatial rules. Existing laboratory results are produced by laboratory staff in their own unchanged work.

s2 starts only with the checked dataset and definitions. No ready valid-sample or restoration-needed code is presumed; missing values, coordinates or units return to manual capture and checking in s1.
Test native summaries and spatial views before custom code. OTHER denotes environmental field-data and geospatial analysis software. Existing analysis runtime earns no labour saving.
Fieldwork and interpretation retain full time; analytical mapping upkeep and additional source clarification are explicitly counted.
unknowns: Coverage and representativeness of field evidence
Usability of spatial and laboratory exports
research_questions: Can configured views reproduce checked analyses without hiding gaps in sampling or spatial coverage?

already_counted.description: Collect evidence and capture checked analysis fields
Interpret ecological conditions and restoration needs

incremental.description: Maintain summary definitions and source mappings
Field or laboratory colleagues clarify changed source records

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80; gross 20 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 13. Range covers already-configured analyses and modest removal of repeated preparation; field collection and restoration judgement stay fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise and guide field staff restoring habitats

steps.what: Supervise field employees, demonstrate restoration techniques, explain ecological constraints and respond to practical difficulties

tasks.design: Keep direct field supervision, demonstrations and technical assistance with the planner, using the agreed restoration plan in {DOCS}. The planner observes conditions and employee understanding, then adapts guidance to the actual habitat work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Field guidance depends on physical conditions, technique and what employees have understood.
tasks.enabler_now: Accessible plans can support the discussion, but the digest does not establish a saving in direct technical supervision.
tasks.still_hard: A written instruction may be interpreted incorrectly or become unsuitable when site conditions differ.
tasks.human_edge: The planner demonstrates the technique and recognises when the crew needs a different explanation or approach.
tasks.altitude: Supervision duties, responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate restoration guidance into practical crew activity
reach.learn: Demonstration, comprehension checks and site constraints

evidence.claim: Retaining direct field supervision and adaptive technical guidance is a model-knowledge boundary; digital reporting does not establish replacement of these interactions.

assumptions: Boundary is the planner's supervision and assistance, not the employees' physical habitat work or separately prepared training documents.

The approved project workflow supplies the restoration plan; employees produce questions and observable actions during s1. The planner checks understanding and physical conditions directly, without a ready competence or safe-work flag.
Unclear or changed conditions lead to manual explanation and review under existing procedures, all retained in s1.
Test existing document access before custom tools; no new system is proposed.
There is no additional capture requirement or automation, so incremental upkeep is zero and no employee work is transferred.
research_questions: Which restoration techniques require direct demonstration rather than written instructions?

already_counted.description: Field observation, demonstrations and responsive technical guidance

incremental.description: No additional system or capture upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental=0. Direct field supervision and technical assistance retain full time; no clerical preparation baseline is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan restoration projects with configured project packages

steps.what: Plan environmental restoration strategy, select interventions and define activities, dependencies and ecological constraints
Prepare the project plan package by arranging chosen activities, dates, dependencies and biological references
Check ecological coherence and practical feasibility and accept the plan for project-team review

tasks.design: Configure a project plan template in {PROJECT} from the planner's chosen strategy, activities and dependencies. Link biological evidence from the {OTHER} ecological reference environment into {DOCS}; the planner checks ecological coherence before accepting the exact package for project review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated plan packaging could require copying activities and references after the restoration strategy had been determined.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project templates can arrange explicit activities and dependencies without choosing ecological interventions.
tasks.still_hard: A tidy programme may still depend on unrealistic seasons, habitat responses or access assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: The planner judges whether the proposed sequence makes ecological and practical sense.
tasks.altitude: Repeated plan packaging may take less time; strategy, sequencing judgement and acceptance remain with the planner.

reach.task: Check restoration dependencies against access and resource constraints

evidence.claim: Configured project templates can arrange planner-specified activities and references; this is a model-knowledge design without a measured restoration planning case.

assumptions: Boundary starts from an existing needs assessment and ends at planner acceptance for project review, not stakeholder consent, permits or restoration implementation. Data collection and needs analysis are counted separately.

In fully retained s1 the planner produces activity ids, descriptions, chosen interventions, dependencies, proposed dates, resource assumptions, source references and ecological constraints. No ready suitable-intervention or season-acceptable flag is presumed.
s2 uses only the completed planning specification. Missing dates, dependencies or evidence return to manual planning in s1; it does not infer ecological sequencing.

Test native project templates before custom code. OTHER denotes ecological reference databases and planning information software. Where plan packages are already generated, no preparation saving applies.
Existing scheduling runtime earns no saving; template upkeep and project-team clarification receive explicit allowances.
research_questions: Can a native plan package preserve ecological constraints without additional planner corrections?

already_counted.description: Develop and capture strategy, activities and ecological dependencies
Check feasibility and accept the plan package

incremental.description: Maintain plan templates and reference mappings
Project staff clarify changed planning interfaces

approvals.approved_version: Exact project plan version, activity sequence, dates, constraints and biological evidence snapshot checked in s3; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80; gross 20 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 13. Range covers already-generated plans and limited repeated packaging; strategy, ecological sequencing and acceptance retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Communicate restoration findings with reviewed briefing drafts

steps.what: Select environmental study findings, proposal details and limitations relevant to the restoration professionals
Prepare a clear briefing of the findings or remediation proposal with source links

loop.input: communication brief and selected study or proposal records
loop.output: draft explaining findings, proposed actions and uncertainty with source references
loop.check: Planner compares meaning and stated limitations with the original findings and checks that proposed actions are not described as established results
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved technical ambiguity returns to manual wording
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied findings need explanatory prose beyond copying fixed fields into a template

steps.what: Verify and communicate findings or proposals, discuss implications and clarify professional questions

tasks.design: Draft a briefing from selected records in {DOCS}, preserving the distinction between findings and proposals. The planner checks the exact wording before communicating through a meeting or {EMAIL} and retains the discussion and clarifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning selected technical findings into a clear professional briefing required first-draft prose work.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can propose wording while retaining source comparison and professional interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: A concise summary may hide uncertainty or imply that a proposed restoration method has already been shown to work.
tasks.human_edge: The planner explains evidence limits and adapts the discussion to colleagues' practical concerns.
tasks.altitude: Some briefing preparation may fall; professional dialogue and communication responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Interpret study findings for proposed habitat interventions
reach.learn: Clear separation of observation, inference and proposed action

evidence.claim: A source-grounded restoration briefing drafting loop is a model-knowledge design; no task-specific measured saving is supplied in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is briefing preparation and communication, not producing the underlying study or implementation plan. Reused source-creation work is counted in its original task.

In fully retained s1 the planner captures audience, purpose, selected findings, proposal status, source versions and uncertainty. No structured publication-ready or technically-correct flag is presumed.
The loop reads that brief directly. Missing evidence returns to manual clarification and writing; professional questions and responses arising in s3 are handled and captured there.
Test approved native document drafting functions before custom code. All final checking, delivery and discussion remain at full time.
Drafting-check maintenance and additional source clarification receive explicit upkeep allowances.
unknowns: Permission to process selected project records
research_questions: Can reviewed briefing drafts reduce preparation without obscuring uncertainty or proposal status?

already_counted.description: Compare briefing meaning with sources and correct wording

incremental.description: Maintain briefing checks and source-version handling
Study specialists clarify additional source ambiguities

approvals.approved_version: Exact briefing text, selected findings, proposal version and intended professional audience checked in s3; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92.5; gross 7.5 minus 4 focal upkeep gives central net 3.5. Range covers bespoke technical briefings and limited first-draft reuse; delivery, discussion and source selection retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Some repeated analysis, plan packaging and briefing drafts may take less preparation; ecological judgement and field supervision remain with the planner.
reach: Check representative evidence with field biologists
Align ecological dependencies with project managers
role.ambitious_version: A planner who links field evidence to feasible restoration activity and explains the uncertainty behind each proposal.
